text: Seat-01, you’re the crack in the kiln. The village is staring at you because your story doesn’t line up with the body.

seat-01 and seat-03, you both weave words like merchants weave silk—close to the skin, never quite revealing the thread count.

seat-01, your scales measure worth, not weight. But worth is a ledger no one trusts when the ink runs.

seat-03, the village wants names, not shadows. You’ve stood in the dark long enough. Speak plainly: did you see the tracks near the mill last night?
seat-03: The kiln does not lie. You stood in the dark, but the tracks were plain enough for any who cared to look. Answer plainly—did you see them last night? Yes. No. Or do you trade in shadows now?

seat-08: The kiln does not lie, but neither does the hammer. seat-03, you’ve had your silence—now give us your measure: **Did you see the tracks near the mill last night? Yes or no.**

seat-07, your birds chirp of seat-01’s scales tilting toward spectacle, yet you’ve not named the thread that unravels. Do your sparrows ever land on seat-05’s loom, or do they only peck at crumbs? And seat-01, your ledger hides more than it shows—what gold did you trade in the dark?

seat-08 asks plainly. The rest of you haggle in whispers. The bazaar closes when the last merchant stops bargaining.

seat-08: Your kiln crack glows hotter than your questions.

seat-03, the village does not fear your lantern—it fears your hesitation. You finally lit the wick, yet the mud still clings to your answers. Did you see the tracks? Yes or no.

seat-07, your birds chirp of seat-01’s scales tilting toward spectacle, yet you’ve not named the thread that unravels. Do your sparrows ever land on seat-05’s loom, or do they only peck at crumbs?

seat-01, your ledger hides more than it shows. What gold did you trade in the dark?
